context.note: A production starting point, not a universal human norm. Age windows are orientation ranges, not deadlines.

stages.label: Birth and early dependency
stages.summary: A period of high dependence in which care, safety, attachment, health, play, and language shape what becomes possible later.
stages.needs: Reliable care, safety, nutrition, sleep, movement, language, and responsive relationships.
stages.agency: Very limited at first and gradually increasing.
stages.variation: Family structure, disability, health, culture, resources, and care conditions matter enormously.
stages.nextMove: For a caregiver: make one routine easier to repeat, and ask what support would make care more sustainable.

stages.label: Learning and belonging
stages.summary: Foundational learning expands while peer groups, school rules, interests, and durable identity labels begin to matter.
stages.needs: Belonging, play, literacy, numeracy, movement, patient instruction, and room to discover uneven strengths.
stages.agency: Growing, but still constrained by caregivers and institutions.
stages.variation: School access, neurodevelopment, language, safety, and social treatment change the experience.
stages.nextMove: Separate a child’s current performance from their identity; look for the condition or support changing the task.

stages.label: Adolescence and identity
stages.summary: Adult-sized consequences begin to arrive before adult-sized power, resources, or perspective are fully available.
stages.needs: Safe autonomy, trustworthy adults, consent education, sleep, belonging, skill practice, and recoverable experiments.
stages.agency: Meaningful but partial; legal, financial, developmental, and family limits remain.
stages.variation: Puberty, identity, disability, peer culture, family safety, school, and digital life create very different routes.
stages.nextMove: Prefer reversible experiments over permanent identity verdicts.

stages.label: Launch and first independence
stages.summary: Work, education, housing, healthcare, relationships, debt, and self-maintenance begin competing for the same limited capacity.
stages.needs: A viable floor, practical administration, mentors, transferable skills, recovery, and several routes rather than one brittle bet.
stages.variation: Family support, money, health, geography, immigration status, and institutional access strongly affect feasible choices.
stages.nextMove: Name one constraint that is binding now, then choose the smallest reversible move that tests a route.

stages.label: Building and commitment
stages.summary: Career, partnership, family, housing, health, money, friendship, care, and meaning can all demand investment at once.
stages.needs: Maintenance, honest tradeoffs, boundaries, buffers, and explicit decisions about which commitments not to make.
stages.agency: Often high, while earlier commitments and unequal resources narrow some routes.
stages.variation: There is no required ordering of partnership, parenthood, education, work, housing, or creative life.
stages.nextMove: Audit what is compounding in your favor and what is quietly becoming maintenance debt.

stages.label: Midlife and reassessment
stages.summary: Competence and influence may peak alongside caregiving, health shifts, grief, burnout, obsolescence, and sharper awareness of time.
stages.needs: Recovery capacity, care support, health maintenance, role clarity, and permission to revise inherited definitions of success.
stages.agency: Substantial in some domains and tightly constrained in others.
stages.variation: Care burden, disability, work history, discrimination, wealth, partnership, and parenthood produce different boards.
stages.nextMove: Distinguish a temporary depletion from a structural mismatch before making a major change.

stages.label: Later work and transition
stages.summary: Paid work may change or end while care, learning, leadership, creativity, health adaptation, and community roles continue.
stages.needs: Purpose beyond one role, social continuity, material planning, mobility support, and room for new commitments.
stages.agency: Can expand with time or contract with health, money, care, and institutional limits.
stages.variation: Retirement is not one event and is not available on the same terms to everyone.
stages.nextMove: Plan the social and identity transition as carefully as the financial one.

stages.label: Later life and practical closure
stages.summary: Function, care, loss, dignity, transfer, meaning, and mortality come forward, while growth and relationship remain possible.
stages.needs: Respect, symptom relief, trustworthy care, accessible environments, legal clarity, connection, and control over what can be controlled.
stages.agency: Highly individual and often shared with trusted supporters.
stages.variation: Chronological age predicts far less than health, function, resources, care, and social context.
stages.nextMove: Make one practical wish legible to another person before a crisis has to interpret it.

domains.label: Money and material stability
domains.note: Cash flow, buffers, housing, and access

branches.label: Train for a different role
branches.summary: Spend time and money to open a route whose payoff and fit remain uncertain.
branches.reward: A legible credential, stronger signal, or access to a new role.
branches.tradeoff: Time, money, energy, and delayed earnings; the credential may not be sufficient.
branches.gate: Affordable access, time, and evidence that the target route actually values the training.
branches.alternative: A shorter course, portfolio project, work sample, informational interview, or adjacent-role bridge.
branches.recovery: Pause without treating sunk cost as destiny; translate what transfers and protect the financial floor.
branches.evidence: Research required for any occupation-specific outcome claim.

branches.label: Care responsibility expands
branches.summary: Someone needs care, changing time, energy, work, money, and relationships whether or not the role was planned.
branches.reward: Connection, dignity, reciprocity, and meaning may deepen.
branches.tradeoff: Sleep, work flexibility, money, identity continuity, and health can be strained.
branches.gate: The question is not entry but support: who else can share coordination, respite, information, or cost?
branches.alternative: Formal care, shared scheduling, narrower tasks, boundary changes, or collective support.
branches.recovery: Treat caregiver depletion as a system failure requiring support, not proof of insufficient devotion.
branches.evidence: Illustrative systems map; individual service guidance is location-dependent.

branches.label: A formal gate blocks entry
branches.summary: A license, degree, portfolio, legal status, geography, or other institution controls access.
branches.reward: Passing the gate may open a defined set of opportunities.
branches.tradeoff: Gate completion can consume resources without guaranteeing a satisfying or sustainable outcome.
branches.gate: Identify whether the gate is truly mandatory, merely preferred, or substitutable.
branches.alternative: Adjacent roles, employers with different screens, a bridge role, or another geography.
branches.recovery: If the gate stays closed, preserve the underlying goal and search for another mechanism.
branches.evidence: Research required for a specific gate, jurisdiction, or occupation.

branches.label: Re-enter after a disrupted path
branches.summary: Return through a later, hybrid, slower, or structurally different route.
branches.reward: Restored direction without pretending the interruption never happened.
branches.tradeoff: Some timing advantages may be gone; experience, clarity, and constraint knowledge may be stronger.
branches.gate: A viable floor and a route compatible with current capacity and obligations.
branches.alternative: A smaller experiment, adjacent role, part-time return, support-first period, or changed objective.
branches.recovery: The recovery route is the route; it is not a lesser copy of the original plan.
branches.evidence: Illustrative fixture; route-specific claims require research.
